summary: Defines a YANG module for performance monitoring of both underlay networks and overlay VPN services. It builds on the network topology model of RFC 8345 so that measurements can be tied to topology at each layer.

eli5.summary: A report card for a network and for the private connections running over it, in a format computers can easily read.

subtitle: A YANG model that reports delay, loss, jitter and interface counters for both a network and the VPN services running on it.

tldr.problem: The performance of a VPN service depends on the underlay network that carries it, but there was no common data model to report both layers together on one topology.
tldr.mechanism: The ietf-network-vpn-pm YANG module augments the RFC 8345 network topology model with network-level, node-level, link-level and termination-point-level performance data, including loss, delay and jitter statistics.
tldr.outcome: A controller or orchestrator can read network and VPN performance in one standard shape, on demand or by subscription. The module defines no new metrics or measurement methods.

today: RFC 9375 is a Proposed Standard published in April 2023. Neither an obsoleting nor an updating RFC is recorded for it.

sections.title: Why Monitor Network and VPN Together
sections.content:
The performance of a VPN service is tied to the performance of the underlay network that carries it. The RFC gives examples: link delay between Provider Edge (PE) and Provider (P) devices, and packet loss on the Layer 2 and Layer 3 interfaces that connect PEs to Customer Edge (CE) devices, both directly affect VPN service performance.

RFC 9375 therefore defines one YANG module for performance monitoring (PM) of both layers. It is built as an augmentation of the network topology model in RFC 8345 and uses types from RFC 9181, among others. The RFC states plainly that it introduces no new metrics and no new measurement mechanisms; it reuses existing ones. The base model can be extended with technology-specific details, such as Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) statistics.
sections.eli5: If your video call to a friend is bad, you want to know whether the problem is the road or the car. This model lets one report cover both the road and the cars on it.

sections.title: How the Model Is Used
sections.content:
The model sits between a service orchestrator (or another OSS/BSS client) and a network controller, as in the layered architecture of RFC 8309. Before using it, the controller needs topology visibility, for example from RFC 8345 for networks or from the L3VPN and L2VPN network models for VPNs. The controller then builds network or VPN performance data by aggregating and filtering lower-level counters collected from devices.

The RFC lists example data sources: OWAMP, TWAMP, STAMP, MPLS loss and delay measurement, and IOAM. The model also defines network-wide measurement intervals so that requirements can be aligned across a network or a VPN service.

The module only describes how results are reported. How the numbers are measured is left to those existing methods.
sections.eli5: A boss asks a manager for a progress report, and the manager collects numbers from lots of workers. This model is the form the manager fills in.

sections.title: Subscribing or Asking On Demand
sections.content:
There are two ways to collect the data. Applications that need a continuous view, such as service assurance, can use the YANG-Push subscription model of RFC 8641. On-change notifications fit topology updates, a periodic notification gives real-time performance data, a replay notification can fetch history from devices that keep it, and alarm notifications can flag metrics that cross a threshold.

For a one-off snapshot, an application can read the data through NETCONF (RFC 6241) or RESTCONF. For example, a specified link-id of a VPN can be used as a filter in a RESTCONF GET request to retrieve per-link VPN PM data.
sections.eli5: You can either sign up for a text message every few seconds, or you can walk up and ask for the score right now.

sections.title: Network and Node Levels
sections.content:
The module is named ietf-network-vpn-pm and augments ietf-network and ietf-network-topology. Underlay networks and VPN services appear as separate entries in the network list. A service presence container tells them apart: when it is absent, the entry is about the network itself; when present, it is about a VPN service whose kind is given by service-type, such as L3VPN or VPLS.

At network level, vpn-id ties the data to the service configuration, and vpn-service-topology says whether the VPN is any-to-any, hub-spoke (hubs can exchange traffic) or hub-spoke-disjoint (hubs cannot).

At node level, node-type records whether a device is a PE, a P or an ASBR. A read-only entry-summary lists IPv4 route counts, IPv6 route counts and MAC entry counts, each as a maximum and a total of active entries. For VPN topologies, role gives the node's role, such as hub or spoke.
sections.eli5: Each building in a city gets a label saying what kind it is and how many rooms it has, and each neighborhood says which club it belongs to.

sections.title: Link and Termination Point Statistics
sections.content:
Links carry the main metrics, in a perf-mon container. All are unidirectional. Each measurement has a start-time, an end-time, a pm-source (for example BGP-LS, OWAMP, TWAMP, STAMP, Y.1731 or IOAM) and one-way loss, delay and jitter statistics. Delay and jitter can be reported as minimum and maximum values or as percentiles. A parallel list reports the same statistics per class-id, a class of service name internal to the administration.

Clients choose percentiles with low-percentile, intermediate-percentile and high-percentile. Setting one to 0.000 says the client is not interested in it; setting all three to zero means only peak and minimum values are reported. The measurement-interval is in seconds, with a default of 60.

For VPN links, vpn-pm-type chooses between inter-vpn-access-interface PM (logical point-to-point connections between VPN access interfaces) and vpn-tunnel PM. Usually only one of the two is used.

Termination points have a read-only pm-statistics container with inbound and outbound counters (octets, unicast, broadcast, multicast, discards, errors, and inbound unknown protocol) and a last-updated time. A vpn-network-access list repeats the counters per VPN network access when several accesses share one physical port.
sections.eli5: For each road between two towns, the model records how many cars got lost, how long the trip took and how bumpy it was. For each gate it counts cars going in and out.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module is meant to be accessed through NETCONF or RESTCONF, whose mandatory-to-implement secure transports are SSH and TLS respectively. The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM, RFC 8341) can restrict users to a subset of operations and content.

Writable data nodes can be sensitive. Unauthorized writes can lead to inaccurate or incomplete measurements. The RFC lists examples: changing the service type or VPN identifier can disable VPN PM, changing percentiles affects reporting cadence, and changing the measurement interval or vpn-pm-type affects monitoring fidelity. Read access to node, link statistics and termination point statistics can disclose operational state of networks or VPNs, so read access also needs control. The module defines no RPC operations or actions.
sections.eli5: Only trusted people should be allowed to change the report settings or read the report, because a wrong setting gives a wrong picture.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA has registered the XML namespace URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-network-vpn-pm and the YANG module ietf-network-vpn-pm with the prefix nvp, referencing RFC 9375.
sections.eli5: The module got its own official name in a public list so nobody else uses it.
